title: R and U
summary: Two new keys: R and U. The finger goes out, presses, and comes back.
intro: Two new keys in this lesson: R and U. They belong to your left middle finger and your right middle finger. The movement is always the same — out, press, back — and the way back is the part being trained, because a finger left out of place spoils the next letter.
congrats: Two more keys under your fingers. If R and U already come without searching, the lesson has done its job.

screens.text: This key belongs to your left middle finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only R and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.
screens.content:
r r
rht n rh
r r rr

screens.text: This key belongs to your right middle finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only U and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.
screens.content:
ur ru
trh un tr
ru ur ruru

screens.text: Short groups, one after another. Keep going to the end even if you miss one.
The new keys mixed with the old ones, which is how they will turn up inside words.
screens.content:
tttt rrrr nnnn uuu
rururu ururur
nurt tunr

screens.text: Real words with the new keys. Type each word in one go, not letter by letter.
screens.content:
rush guess grass years
others agree tear stories
user grease roots hours

screens.text: A burst of short words with the new keys in them.
Now the weight is on R, the one you have pressed least.
screens.content:
tears set tight rises
rate ran grease rain
night eggs street sugar

screens.text: Back to patterns for a moment, to check that the fingers still find their way home.
screens.content:
rrrr uuuu
rururu ururur
ru ur

screens.text: Everything you have, mixed together. Notice how many words already come without thinking.
